_comment: What each capability term in this corpus's ROLE.md `tools_allowed`
actually requires, stated in the harness's tool vocabulary.
A role declared `tools_allowed: [stdlib, offline-file-processing]` and a
harness declared `fs_write:ask, network:deny`. Two vocabularies, two
repositories, and nothing that read both -- so the reconciliation rule
lived only in whoever last thought about it. This file is this corpus
making its request in the harness's own words. It grants nothing: the
harness computes min(ceiling, requested) and the ceiling always wins.
WHY THE SOLVER ENTRIES NAME shell_rw AND NOT shell_ro
An external solver writes its results. Classing it as read-only because
it happens to write into a scratch directory would be a permission the
system cannot enforce, described as one it can. A harness ceiling that
denies shell_rw therefore blocks these roles' solver step, and that is
the truthful outcome -- visible in `make permissions-report`, changeable
in exactly one line of the harness's edges/tools.allow, and never
A term with an empty requirement is refused by the reader: 'needs
nothing' and 'we have not worked this out yet' serialise identically.
